title: Pasta e Ceci (Pasta and Chickpea Stew with Rosemary)
changes_from_base: Chickpeas replace cannellini or borlotti beans; chilli and lemon added; escarole or kale wilted in; celery and tomato purée left out.
summary: This follows the classic pasta e fagioli method, but uses chickpeas in place of cannellini or borlotti beans, adds chilli and lemon, wilts in escarole or kale, and leaves out the celery and tomato purée.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or casserole (at least 4 litres)

ingredients.item: tinned whole plum tomatoes, drained and crushed
400 g tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed (about 480 g drained)
fine sea salt or table salt
escarole, kale or spinach, roughly chopped

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large heavy saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 5-6 minutes, until softened but not coloured. Keep the heat gentle so the vegetables sweeten slowly rather than catching and turning bitter.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, rosemary and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute, just until fragrant. Keep stirring at this stage, as garlic and rosemary can turn bitter if left too long over direct heat.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and chickpeas
steps.text: Tip in the crushed tomatoes and chickpeas, then crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pot with a spoon or masher. Crushing some of the chickpeas releases their starch into the broth, naturally thickening the stew without any flour or cream.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.text: Pour in the water and add the salt and pepper, then bring to the boil before turning down to a simmer for 10 minutes. This gives the flavours time to come together into a well-seasoned broth before the pasta goes in.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Add the ditalini and simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch on the bottom, until al dente and most of the liquid has been absorbed. For a brothier, soupier stew, stir in a splash more water towards the end.

steps.title: Wilt in the greens
steps.text: Stir in the escarole, kale or spinach and cook just until wilted, then stir through the lemon juice. The brief heat softens the leaves while keeping their colour and a little bite.

steps.title: Serve and finish
steps.text: Ladle into bowls and finish each with a scattering of pecorino and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil. If reheating leftovers, add a splash of water and bring back to a simmer until piping hot throughout (74°C), as the pasta keeps absorbing liquid as it sits.

tips: Crush some of the chickpeas against the pot rather than leaving them all whole; this is what thickens the broth naturally.
Stir often once the pasta goes in - small pasta shapes catch on the bottom of the pot easily as the liquid reduces.
Add the lemon juice at the end, off any high heat, so its brightness doesn't cook away.
Keep a little extra water on hand when reheating, since the pasta keeps soaking up liquid even once it's off the heat.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months (the pasta softens slightly on thawing). Reheat in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
